messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: new line at end of (R)Stan program
parts:
Any idea why there's a problem with new lines in RStan?
We could always pad with a new line. Could you just
pad all programs that don't end in newline with a newline
for doing comparison? Even if you have to add an extra
newline at end, it's no big deal as Stan isn't whitespace
sensitive and it won't affect any of the line number
reports?

- Bob

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: new line at end of (R)Stan program
parts:
On Monday, August 1, 2016 at 4:12:33 PM UTC-4, Bob Carpenter wrote:
Any idea why there's a problem with new lines in RStan?

The md5sum hash is different with and without the terminating new line, so it thinks that a model on disk (without a new line) is different from the model in memory (where a new line is added automatically).

We could always pad with a new line.  Could you just
pad all programs that don't end in newline with a newline
for doing comparison?

Maybe. I was not sure how to check (in a platform independent way) whether a .stan file on disk ends in a new line or not. When it is read as a string into R's memory, that information is gone.

Ben

messages.subject: Re: new line at end of (R)Stan program
parts: If that can't be checked, then what about immediately adding a new line to all Stan programs when they are passed to RStan? For some it will mean ending in two empty lines, but that doesn't really matter.
